hook: The Dutch master of light and shadow, who painted himself nearly 100 times.

pages.x: Rembrandt van Rijn was born in Leiden in 1606, the son of a miller. He left university at 14 to train as a painter, and at 25 moved to Amsterdam, the booming centre of world trade, where he became the most fashionable portrait painter in town.
At 26 he made his name with The Anatomy Lesson of Dr Tulp, a group portrait of surgeons leaning in to watch a dissection. Other painters lined people up like statues; his are alive.
pages.img: The Anatomy Lesson of Dr. Nicolaes Tulp

pages.x: He married Saskia van Uylenburgh, a rich young woman, and painted her again and again. They bought a grand house and he spent wildly on art and curiosities. Three of their children died as babies; only their son Titus lived. Saskia died in 1642.

In 1642 he finished The Night Watch, a huge painting of a city militia marching out, full of light, shadow and movement that no group portrait had had before. It is not really a night scene: the varnish darkened over the years.

Out of fashion and deep in debt, he went bankrupt in 1656, and his house and collection were sold. He lived on in a rented house with his companion Hendrickje and his son Titus, and kept painting. Both died before him.
He painted, drew and etched himself nearly 100 times, from a curly-haired young man to a lined, weary old one: a diary of a life in pictures. He died in 1669, poor, and was buried in a rented grave.
Rembrandt is the greatest painter of the Dutch golden age and one of the greatest ever, a master of light and shadow and of showing what people feel inside.
pts: A master of light and shadow
